topics.title: Sizing, Units & Functions
topics.summary: Choose units based on what a value should respond to, then use min(), max(), clamp(), and calc() to express relationships instead of magic numbers.

concepts.name: Relative units
concepts.explanation: rem responds to the root font size, em responds to the current element, percentages depend on a reference size, and viewport units respond to the viewport.

concepts.name: Content constraints
concepts.explanation: min-width, max-width, min-height, and max-height let a component be flexible without becoming unusably small or large.

concepts.name: Math functions
concepts.explanation: calc() combines compatible units. min(), max(), and clamp() encode lower/upper bounds and fluid scaling directly in CSS.

topics.challenge: Create a centered container with a maximum width and a heading that scales fluidly using clamp().
topics.hint: Use min() for container width and clamp(min, preferred, max) for the font size.

topics.title: Positioning, Containing Blocks & z-index
topics.summary: Control normal flow, offsets, sticky/fixed behavior, and stacking without using positioning as a substitute for layout.

concepts.name: Position modes
concepts.explanation: relative keeps the element in normal flow while allowing offsets; absolute removes it from normal flow and positions it against a containing block; fixed attaches to a viewport-like reference.

concepts.name: Sticky
concepts.explanation: position: sticky behaves like relative until a threshold such as top: 0 is crossed, then remains stuck within its scroll container.

concepts.name: Stacking
concepts.explanation: z-index participates in stacking contexts. A huge z-index cannot escape an ancestor stacking context; first understand which element created the context.

topics.challenge: Place a badge in the top-right of a card and make a sidebar sticky.
topics.hint: The absolute badge needs a positioned ancestor; give the card position: relative.

topics.title: CSS Grid Fundamentals
topics.summary: Use explicit rows and columns, flexible tracks, named areas, and item placement for two-dimensional layouts.

concepts.name: Tracks
concepts.explanation: grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows define tracks. fr shares leftover space; minmax() gives a track flexible limits.

concepts.name: Placement
concepts.explanation: Items can be placed with grid-column/grid-row or named areas. Auto-placement handles the rest of the items.

concepts.name: Responsive grids
concepts.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) can create grids that adapt to available width without a breakpoint for every card count.

topics.challenge: Create an auto-fitting card grid using minmax() and make one item span two columns.
topics.hint: A useful responsive pattern is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(minimum, 1fr)).

topics.title: Media Queries & Responsive Strategy
topics.summary: Choose breakpoints when content needs them, and query user preferences and interaction capabilities in addition to width.

concepts.name: Content breakpoints
concepts.explanation: Resize until the design stops working, then add a breakpoint. Device-name breakpoints age poorly because real devices vary.

concepts.name: Preference queries
concepts.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-color-scheme let your interface respect system-level user preferences.

concepts.name: Capability queries
concepts.explanation: hover and pointer media features can help avoid hover-only experiences on touch-oriented devices.

topics.challenge: Add one layout breakpoint and one prefers-reduced-motion rule.
topics.hint: Responsive CSS is not only about width. Treat accessibility preferences as responsive inputs too.

topics.title: Transforms, Transitions & State Feedback
topics.summary: Animate state changes efficiently with transforms and opacity while keeping motion purposeful and accessible.

concepts.name: Transforms
concepts.explanation: transform can translate, scale, rotate, or skew an element without changing normal document flow.

concepts.name: Transitions
concepts.explanation: transition animates between old and new computed values when a property changes. Prefer naming properties instead of transition: all.

concepts.name: State design
concepts.explanation: Hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and selected states should communicate meaning. Motion should support state feedback rather than distract from it.

topics.challenge: Create a button hover/focus transition using transform and one other visual property.
topics.hint: Animate a small set of deliberate properties and include :focus-visible, not only :hover.
